source: App Hub issue #172, the host-API family table and its addendum (https://github.com/OctoSense-org/OctoSense-App-Hub/issues/172#issuecomment-6073188277, https://github.com/OctoSense-org/OctoSense-App-Hub/issues/172#issuecomment-6073269227)

families.served_to_detail: The notice service: ai-providers.notify only, os.ai-providers only. Unreachable in practice: no capability names it and App Hub refuses the hyphenated tool namespace, so os.ai-providers cannot declare the tool.

Connections are stored per calling app id. auth.connect needs the app's admitted manifest to grant `auth`, plus `github`, `gcalendar` or `gmail` for those scopes (the shell's scope check). auth.backend.me and auth.backend.request since rc.1. connect, select and disconnect are foreground only; accounts, active and backend.* are agent-allowed.

may_call: app id starts with `os.`. No manifest can declare `cad` (not in KNOWN_CAPABILITIES at ba36df05). Registered under `feature = "app-hub"`, which both packages enable by default, so by the gates on all six native targets; the code comment says desktop only and ADR 0013 leaves phone packaging open (phone unverified).

os.calendar only ("calendar is Calendar's own service"). os.calendar's agent reaches it as its own namespace; Mail's agent is offered calendar.events, calendar.add_event and calendar.notify, which still run as os.calendar. The capability exists from contract 1.5.0 (beta.2); a store app that declares it is refused by the service.

Any admitted app whose manifest grants `camera` and declares requires: ["host-api-v1"]; then per-app consent on a host sheet and the OS permission. permission.status and permission.revoke are agent-allowed, permission.request is foreground only. Registered on every app-hub shell, but descriptors and permission support exist on Android and macOS only. Before rc.1 the string was os.camera's notice namespace on phone builds (camera.notify, os.camera only); see the collision note.
Declarable capability with an install-time permission label; no service serves the family on any ref.

The calling app's own authorized connection (`auth` to connect). Methods calendars, cached, refresh, get, prepare; review_save; review_save is foreground only, needs the native review hook and is described for macOS and Android only.

The calling app's own authorized connection (`auth` to connect). Methods repositories, files, read; review_save; review_save is foreground only, needs the native review hook and is described for macOS and Android only.

Caller is the runner's app id, treated as granted unless the call comes from a host sheet (the service relies on the isolate's `glance` gate); no os.* check. Methods publish, withdraw, list; take_open (since beta.2) only from the foreground app.

The calling app's own authorized Google connection. Methods labels, messages, message, draft.open, draft.get, draft.edit, event.status, events.status, event.decide; draft.review is foreground only, needs the native review hook, macOS and Android only.

Refuses any app id not starting with `os.`; llm.connect_client (and its sheet's client_* methods) only for os.ai-providers. Registered by ai-host's `llm` feature, which the shell's app-hub feature turns on and native mobile always has.

Any admitted app whose manifest grants `location` and declares requires: ["host-api-v1"]; then per-app consent on a host sheet and the OS permission. permission.status and permission.revoke are agent-allowed, permission.request is foreground only. Registered on every app-hub shell, but descriptors and permission support exist on Android and macOS only. location.get (last-known fix) is described and served on Android only.

store: accounts, add_account, remove_account, folders, sync, peek, skip_event, list, message, mark_read, notify, for any app granted `mail`, each account bound to the app ids that signed it in; send is always refused (review flow). os.mail only since beta.2: publish_card, propose_reply, draft, suggest_reply, propose_send, review_send. At beta.1 every method was store.
The notice service (one per system app whose namespace has no service): maps.notify only, os.maps only. Reached by os.maps's agent tool as its own namespace; no capability names it.
Not registered as a shell host service; answered only for mini-apps inside the native Rinx app by Rinx's own host.

Any admitted app whose manifest grants `microphone` and declares requires: ["host-api-v1"]; then per-app consent on a host sheet and the OS permission. permission.status and permission.revoke are agent-allowed, permission.request is foreground only. Registered on every app-hub shell, but descriptors and permission support exist on Android and macOS only.

Any admitted app (installed or system) whose manifest lists `model`: from rc.1 the shell's digest-checked admitted bundle (set_model_grants, root must match); at beta.1 and beta.2 the manifest file next to the host dir (manifest_grants). complete and budget since beta.1, with no descriptor; image, audio, embeddings, video, video.status, video.cancel, capabilities since rc.1, described (agent access allowed). Platforms are the media descriptors; complete and budget register on the same six by gate.
may_call: app id starts with `os.`. Methods list, read, topics.get, topics.set, refresh, sources, feeds.import, notify.

Any contained app; per call the person's consent for that app (the shipped gate) and the exact octos.* method in its manifest. No os.* check. Registered only where the shell hosts the octos kernel (cfg(kernel) plus a configured kernel source); iOS has no supported kernel source.

os.photos only. beta.1 to rc.1: the notice service, photos.notify only. main: os.photos's own service under feature app-hub, photos.info (photo engine, area <host dir>/photo) and photos.notify. os.photos reaches it as its own namespace and does not declare `photos`; `photos` is declarable from contract 1.5.0 and passes the isolate gate, but makes no store app a caller.

App Hub built-in, answered in dispatch before the service registry; no caller check beyond the isolate's capability gate. Methods runtime.list and runtime.describe, agent access allowed. Describes implemented APIs; grants nothing.

may_call: os.* or the native Sheets app id `sheets` (a reserved name, so never a store app). No manifest can declare `sheet` (not in KNOWN_CAPABILITIES at ba36df05); the live route is the Sheets agent's sheets.* tools, renamed to sheet.* by the shell. Registered under `feature = "app-hub"`, which both packages enable by default, so by the gates on all six native targets; the code comment says desktop only and ADR 0013 leaves phone packaging open (phone unverified).
